title_en: Zhongshan Longcheng Daily Products Co., Ltd. v. Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: 1. An agreement reached in advance between a right holder and an infringer on the amount of damages for infringement does not constitute a transaction contract between the right holder and the infringer. Therefore, the civil liability that the infringer shall bear is solely tort liability, and does not fall under the circumstances of concurrence of liability for tort and liability for breach of contract as stipulated in Article 122 of the Contract Law.

full_text_en:
Zhongshan Longcheng Daily Products Co., Ltd. v. Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

【Ruling Summary】

1. The prior agreement between the right holder and the infringer on the amount of damages for infringement does not constitute a transaction contract between them. Therefore, the civil liability to be borne by the infringer is solely tort liability, and does not fall under the circumstance of concurrence of tort liability and liability for breach of contract as stipulated in Article 122 of the Contract Law of the PRC.

2. The prior agreement between the right holder and the infringer on the amount of damages for infringement is a method of calculation pre-agreed by the parties on the losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement or the profits gained by the infringer from infringement in the event of future infringement. In the absence of circumstances such as invalidity provided by law, a people's court may directly use the prior agreement between the right holder and the infringer as the basis for determining the amount of damages for infringement.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment
No. 116 (2013) Min Ti

Petitioner for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhongshan Longcheng Daily Products Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 28 Kuixing Avenue, Dongsheng Town, Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Huang Yingyuan, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Deng Qingzheng, Lawyer of Guangdong Jinjian Shikong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd. Domicile: Chengdong Development Zone, Hanchuan City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Wu Jiawen, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jianhua, Staff of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Caihua, Lawyer of Beijing Yingke (Wuhan) Law Firm.

The Petitioner for Retrial, Zhongshan Longcheng Daily Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longcheng Company), filed a petition for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment No. 86 (2012) E Min San Zhong Zi of the Hubei High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of utility model patent with the Respondent, Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tongba Company). On April 2, 2013, this Court issued Civil Ruling No. 12 (2013) Min Shen Zi, granting a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on October 17, 2013. Deng Qingzheng, agent ad litem of Longcheng Company; Chen Jianhua and Sun Caihua, agents ad litem of Tongba Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

In May 2011, Longcheng Company filed a lawsuit with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court, alleging that it was the patent holder of the utility model patent titled "Front Wheel Positioning Device" with patent number ZL01242571.0 (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit). In April 2008, Longcheng Company had filed a lawsuit against Tongba Company with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court for infringement of the patent-in-suit. The court rendered Civil Judgment No. 144 (2008) Wu Zhi Chu Zi, ordering Tongba Company to cease infringement and pay damages. Tongba Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal. During the second instance, upon the court's mediation, the parties reached a mediation agreement, and the Hubei High People's Court issued Civil Mediation Letter No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi, the main content of which was: Tongba Company guaranteed not to infringe Longcheng Company's patent rights again, and if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right was found, Tongba Company would voluntarily compensate Longcheng Company RMB 1,000,000. However, Tongba Company continued to engage in large-scale infringement of Longcheng Company's patent-in-suit. The Notarial Certificate No. 5846 (2009) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi and No. 938 (2010) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi can prove that Tongba Company continued to offer for sale through the internet and actually manufactured and sold infringing products. From October 23 to 25, 2009, Tongba Company participated in the China Import and Export Fair, exhibited infringing products and distributed a large number of product brochures containing pictures of the infringing products. In March 2010, Longcheng Company, through the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province, had the purchase of relevant infringing products notarized. In summary, Longcheng Company requested the court to order Tongba Company to pay RMB 1,000,000 in damages and bear the litigation costs of this case.

Tongba Company argued: After the case No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi was concluded by mediation of the Hubei High People's Court, Longcheng Company used improper means to collect evidence at Tongba Company. In March 2011, Longcheng Company sent a foreign businessman together with notary personnel to Tongba Company to purchase the accused infringing products. The salesperson of Tongba Company told them that there were no accused infringing products, and that since there was an infringement dispute with Longcheng Company, production would have to wait until Longcheng Company's patent expired. However, the other party insisted on ordering, saying that they would take a few samples back first and place large-scale orders after the patent expired. Therefore, the salesperson of Tongba Company provided them with a few samples. In addition, Longcheng Company's claim for RMB 1,000,000 in damages had no legal basis.

The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court found the following facts after trial at first instance:

1. Overview of the patent-in-suit

The filing date of the patent-in-suit is July 10, 2001, the grant date is May 15, 2002, and the annual fees were paid up to July 10, 2011. The original patent holder of the patent-in-suit was Zhongshan Longshun Daily Products Co., Ltd. On July 30, 2004, the patent holder was changed to Longcheng Company. The claims of the patent-in-suit record: 1. A front wheel positioning device, installed at the end of a front leg tube of a baby carriage, characterized in that it comprises: a vertical rotating shaft, the lower end combined with the axle of the front wheel, the upper end pivotally connected to the end of the front leg tube and maintaining a coaxial rotation connection state; and a locking mechanism for controlling whether the front wheel can turn, disposed between the upper end of the vertical rotating shaft and the end of the front leg tube. 2. The front wheel positioning device according to claim 1, characterized in that: the end of the front leg tube has a positioning hole for the locking mechanism to lock into after positioning. 3. The front wheel positioning device according to claim 1, characterized in that: the locking mechanism comprises: a fixing pin; and a lifting mechanism for controlling the lifting or movement of the fixing pin. 4. The front wheel positioning device according to claim 3, characterized in that: the lifting mechanism is a pair of rotating discs, between which there is a helical surface, and one end of the rotating discs is connected to the fixing pin. 5. The front wheel positioning device according to claim 4, characterized in that: one side of the rotating discs is provided with a handle for easy rotation of the rotating discs. On August 11, 2008, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 12067, declaring claims 1-3 of the patent-in-suit invalid, and maintaining the patent-in-suit valid on the basis of claims 4 and 5.

2. Allegations of infringement

On October 16, 2009, Xu Chang, agent ad litem of Longcheng Company, under the supervision of notaries Cai Guohua and Chen Jianbo at the Zhongshan Notary Public Office in Guangdong Province, accessed the Alibaba website (http://china.alibaba.com) via the internet, and from that page, after searching, entered Tongba Company's website (http://chen980412.cn.alibaba.com/), and took screenshots of relevant pages of the website, which included an introduction of Tongba Company and photos of various models of baby strollers. The Zhongshan Notary Public Office in Guangdong Province issued Notarial Certificate No. 5846 (2009) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi for the above process. On February 24, 2010, Lin Yanying, agent ad litem of Longcheng Company, under the supervision of notary Cai Guohua at the Zhongshan Notary Public Office in Guangdong Province, accessed Tongba Company's website (http://www.tongba888.cn) via the internet, browsed the introduction of Tongba Company and photos of various models of baby strollers, and took screenshots. The Zhongshan Notary Public Office in Guangdong Province issued Notarial Certificate No. 938 (2010) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi for the above process. The screenshots of Tongba Company's webpages made in the above two notarial certificates did not contain content of the accused infringing products. On March 10, 2010, the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province issued Notarial Certificate No. 125 (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi, which recorded: Citizen Lin Yanying stated that due to work needs, she purchased a carton of a baby stroller from Tongba Company. To prevent disputes, on March 9, 2010, she applied to the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province for evidence preservation by photographing the process of taking out the baby stroller from the defendant and the baby stroller inside the carton. On the same day, notary Cai Junping and notarial staff Xu Juan of the notary office went together with Lin Yanying to the door of Tongba Company. Lin Yanying took out one carton of a baby stroller with carton model TBT85-670# from Tongba Company. The carton was transported to the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province, where it was opened, photographed, and then sealed. On March 9, 2010, Tongba Company issued a sales settlement slip signed by the invoicer Chen Lihua to Longcheng Company, which stated that the model of the product sold was TB85. During evidence examination and the trial, the collegial panel unsealed the accused infringing baby stroller sealed by Notarial Certificate No. 125 (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi of the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province. Both parties had no objection to the sealing condition. The carton of the accused infringing baby stroller showed model TBT85-670#. After unsealing, there was no instruction manual or certificate of conformity or any other materials for the accused infringing baby stroller inside the carton. Tongba Company stated in court that the model of the baby stroller should be determined by the actual baby stroller inside the carton. After unsealing, Longcheng Company compared and believed that the accused infringing product fully fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. Tongba Company acknowledged Longcheng Company's comparison opinion.

3. Status of relevant case handling

On April 2, 2008, Longcheng Company filed a civil lawsuit with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that Tongba Company infringed its patent-in-suit. On June 16, 2009, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 144 (2008) Wu Zhi Chu Zi, ordering: (1) Tongba Company to immediately cease manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling the B858C-B model stroller product that infringed Longcheng Company's utility model patent for "Front Wheel Positioning Device", and to remove promotional content regarding that model stroller product from Tongba Company's website and product brochures; (2) Tongba Company to pay Longcheng Company RMB 80,000 in damages; (3) Dismiss Longcheng Company's other claims. Tongba Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal. On September 2, 2009, the Hubei High People's Court concluded the case by mediation with Civil Mediation Letter No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi, the content of the mediation agreement was: (1) Tongba Company shall immediately cease manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling the B858C-B model baby stroller product as of the date of signing the mediation agreement, remove pictures of that model baby stroller product on Tongba Company's website and the text and picture introduction of that model baby stroller product in product brochures, and guarantee not to infringe Longcheng Company's patent rights again. If one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's design patent right is found, Tongba Company shall voluntarily pay RMB 500,000 in damages; if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right is found, Tongba Company shall voluntarily pay RMB 1,000,000 in damages; (2) Within ten days from the date of signing the mediation agreement, Tongba Company shall pay Longcheng Company RMB 55,000 for economic losses, and pay RMB 3,300 for first instance case acceptance fee and RMB 30 for evidence preservation fee advanced by Longcheng Company; (3) Both parties waive all other claims based on the facts of this case.

4. Other facts

During the first instance trial, Longcheng Company clarified that this case was brought as a patent infringement lawsuit, not a lawsuit for breach of contract, but it requested the amount of damages for infringement to be calculated according to the liquidated damages standard agreed upon by the parties.

The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court held at first instance that the issues in dispute in this case were: whether Longcheng Company held the patent rights of the patent-in-suit; whether Tongba Company committed the infringing acts; and how to determine Tongba Company's civil liability.

1. Whether Longcheng Company held the patent rights of the patent-in-suit

The patent holder of the utility model patent "Front Wheel Positioning Device" (patent number ZL01242571.0) was originally Zhongshan Longshun Daily Products Co., Ltd., and was changed to Longcheng Company on July 30, 2004. On August 11, 2008, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 12067, declaring claims 1-3 of the patent-in-suit invalid, and maintaining the patent-in-suit valid on the basis of claims 4 and 5. The filing date of the patent-in-suit is July 10, 2001, the annual fees were paid up to July 10, 2011, and the time of infringement proved by notarization in this case was March 9, 2010, which was within the term of validity of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, claims 4 and 5 of the patent-in-suit are protected by law in this case.

2. Whether Tongba Company committed the infringing acts

The Notarial Certificate No. 125 (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi issued by the Hanchuan Notary Public Office in Hubei Province proves that on March 9, 2010, citizen Lin Yanying took out one carton of a baby stroller with carton model TBT85-670# from Tongba Company, and on the same day, Tongba Company issued a sales settlement slip. Moreover, during evidence examination and trial, Tongba Company stated that Longcheng Company had brought a foreign businessman to purchase the accused infringing baby stroller, and admitted that the infringing baby stroller alleged by Longcheng Company was sold by Tongba Company. In view of the nature of Tongba Company's production and operation, its production capacity, and its promotion and introduction of products, combined with other evidence in this case, the first instance court found that Tongba Company engaged in manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product.

Regarding the model of the infringing product alleged by Longcheng Company, Notarial Certificate No. 125 (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi proves that the carton model of the baby stroller taken out by Lin Yanying from Tongba Company was TBT85-670#, but the sales settlement slip issued by Tongba Company stated the model as TB86. The parties had a disagreement over the baby stroller model. During the first instance trial, upon unsealing and inspecting the accused infringing baby stroller sealed by notarization, there was no instruction manual or certificate of conformity or any other materials indicating the baby stroller model inside the carton. Tongba Company stated in court that the baby stroller model should be determined by the actual baby stroller inside the carton. The first instance court compared the actual baby stroller with Tongba Company's product brochure, and found that the actual baby stroller was consistent with the TBT86 model product in the brochure. Therefore, it determined that the model of the baby stroller sealed by notarization for infringement was TBT86.

During the trial, the claims of the patent-in-suit were compared with the accused infringing TBT86 model baby stroller. The technical solution of the TBT86 model baby stroller embodied all the essential technical features recorded in claims 4 and 5 of the patent-in-suit. Tongba Company had no objection that the accused infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, nor did it submit evidence to prove that it had statutory grounds for exemption from liability. Therefore, the TBT86 model baby stroller manufactured and sold by Tongba Company infringed the patent rights of Longcheng Company in the patent-in-suit, and Tongba Company shall bear corresponding civil liability according to law.

Regarding Longcheng Company's allegation of Tongba Company's offering for sale, Longcheng Company submitted Notarial Certificate No. 5846 (2009) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi, Notarial Certificate No. 938 (2010) Zhong Zheng Nei Zi, CDs, the Exhibitor List of the China Import and Export Fair, and Product Brochures to prove that Tongba Company had engaged in offering for sale. Upon examination, the screenshots of Tongba Company's webpages made in the above two notarial certificates and the Exhibitor List did not contain content of the accused infringing baby stroller. Only the Product Brochures had several photos and brief text introductions of baby strollers, which could not be compared with the claims of the patent-in-suit in terms of technical features such as the shape, structure and combination of the baby stroller. Therefore, Longcheng Company's claim that Tongba Company offered for sale the accused infringing product was insufficiently supported by evidence and was not upheld.

3. How to determine Tongba Company's civil liability

Longcheng Company clearly stated in court that this case was a tort action, requesting Tongba Company to bear tort liability for damages, with the compensation standard based on the agreement in Civil Mediation Letter No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi between the parties. The first instance court held that the factual and legal bases for tort civil liability and contractual civil liability are different, arising from different legal relationships. Article 122 of the Contract Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) provides that if a party's breach of contract infringes upon the personal or property rights of the other party, the injured party has the right to choose to claim liability for breach of contract in accordance with the Contract Law or to claim tort liability in accordance with other laws. In this case, since Longcheng Company clearly chose to file a tort action for the alleged infringing acts, the amount of damages should be determined in accordance with the Tort Liability Law. Longcheng Company's argument that this case is a tort action and the compensation standard should be based on the agreement in Civil Mediation Letter No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi conflicts with the above provisions of the Contract Law and was not upheld. In this case, because Longcheng Company asserted a tort action, Tongba Company could not raise a defense regarding the facts of breach of contract and whether the liquidated damages were excessive in a breach of contract action, and the breach of contract action could not be included in the scope of court investigation and debate. The mediation letter issued by the court is an agreement on liability arising from conduct that has already occurred between the parties, and does not have the effect of prejudging and enforcing liability for conduct that has not yet occurred in the future. If a future breach of contract as agreed by the parties in the mediation letter occurs, the breach of contract clause still requires the parties to file a separate lawsuit in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, and the liability for breach of contract will be determined by the people's court after finding the facts of the breach and differentiating the circumstances of the breach. In this case, since Longcheng Company did not assert a breach of contract action, the court does not need to make a judgment on whether the parties have breached the contract and the liability for breach of contract. Therefore, it is not appropriate to simply apply the liquidated damages agreed by the parties. The amount of damages in this case should still be determined based on the nature of Tongba Company's infringement, in accordance with the provisions of the Patent Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) on statutory damages. Tongba Company's defense that Longcheng Company's claim for RMB 1,000,000 in damages was insufficiently supported was established.

Longcheng Company did not submit evidence in this case to prove its actual losses or Tongba Company's profits from infringement. The first instance court applied statutory damages according to law. Considering that the patent-in-suit has now expired, the front wheel positioning device is one of the auxiliary components in the whole accused infringing baby stroller, the selling price of the whole stroller is not high, the sales quantity cannot be determined, and Longcheng Company also acknowledged that the accused infringing baby stroller cannot be purchased in the domestic market, and also taking into account that Tongba Company was a repeat infringer, the first instance court determined to appropriately increase the amount of damages for Tongba Company on the basis of the amount awarded in the previous case.

In summary, the first instance court ruled: (1) Tongba Company to pay Longcheng Company RMB 140,000 in damages; (2) Dismiss Longcheng Company's other claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 13,800 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 18,800, shall be borne by Tongba Company.

Longcheng Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, filed an appeal to the Hubei High People's Court, requesting to set aside the first instance judgment and render a new judgment in accordance with the law. The reasons were: (1) The first instance court's failure to find that Tongba Company engaged in offering for sale constituted an error in fact finding; (2) The first instance court's failure to apply the compensation standard agreed by the parties in Civil Mediation Letter No. 42 (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi constituted an error in application of law.

Tongba Company also refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Hubei High People's Court, requesting the revocation of the first-instance judgment and a judgment in accordance with the law. The reasons were as follows: 1. The first-instance court's factual finding that Tongba Company produced and sold the allegedly infringing product was without basis; 2. The first-instance court compared the TBT86 model baby carriage listed in the product brochure with the physical baby carriage purchased by notarization, thereby determining that the notarially purchased baby carriage was the TBT86 model, which was improper; 3. The first-instance court's award of 140,000 yuan in damages did not comply with the provisions of the Patent Law; 4. The first-instance court's decision that Tongba Company bear all the case acceptance fees was unfair.

Upon further trial, the Hubei High People's Court found that the facts found in the first instance were true and confirmed them in accordance with the law. It was also found that on March 9, 2010, Longcheng Company paid 260 yuan to purchase the TBT86 model baby carriage product involved in the case.

The Hubei High People's Court held in the second instance that, in consideration of the appeal requests and reasons of both parties, the issues in dispute in the second instance were: whether Tongba Company had implemented the alleged infringing acts after signing the mediation agreement with Longcheng Company; and how to determine Tongba Company's civil liability.

(I) Whether Tongba Company had implemented the alleged infringing acts after signing the mediation agreement with Longcheng Company

On September 2, 2009, the parties involved signed a mediation agreement. After the mediation agreement was signed, the infringing facts or acts alleged by Longcheng Company against Tongba Company included three aspects: first, exhibiting infringing products and distributing relevant product brochures at the China Import and Export Fair from October 23 to 25, 2009; second, offering for sale the infringing products through the internet; third, conducting another investigation and evidence collection for the infringing act in March 2010, and obtaining notarization of the physical allegedly infringing product through a notary office.

Longcheng Company submitted four pieces of evidence in the first instance to prove that Tongba Company had engaged in offering for sale, namely, Notarial Certificate (2009) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 5846, Notarial Certificate (2010) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 938, the "List of Exhibitors," and the "Product Brochure." Upon examination, the webpage screenshots in the two notarial certificates did not contain the allegedly infringing baby carriage content, and the submitted webpage pictures themselves were not clear enough; the "List of Exhibitors" only contained the name of Tongba Company; the "Product Brochure" only contained one photo and a brief text introduction of the TBT86 baby carriage, and its source and printing date were unclear. Therefore, the first-instance court's failure to find the offering for sale alleged by Longcheng Company had a factual basis.

Longcheng Company submitted evidence in the first instance, including Notarial Certificate (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi No. 125 and a sales settlement slip, to prove that Tongba Company had produced and sold the allegedly infringing product. Upon examination, Notarial Certificate (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi No. 125 stated "took out one box of baby carriage," the outer side of the packaging box indicated "ITEM NO. TBT85-670#," and the outer packaging box did not indicate a specific production date. Meanwhile, the sales settlement slip indicated one product name as "TB86," and another was unclear. The first-instance court compared the notarially purchased baby carriage with the relevant product model in Tongba Company's product brochure, and found it to be consistent with the "TBT86" model product. Based on this, it could be determined at least that one of the baby carriage models provided by Tongba Company to Longcheng Company on March 9, 2010, was the TBT86 model, but the specific production time of this model was unclear. Since the mediation agreement between the parties was reached on September 2, 2009, the existing evidence submitted by Longcheng Company could not prove that Tongba Company had engaged in production infringement after signing the mediation agreement.

Although the specific production time of the TBT86 model baby carriage product purchased by Longcheng Company through notarization was unclear, Longcheng Company paid a consideration of 260 yuan for it, and Tongba Company issued a corresponding sales settlement slip. At the same time, based on Tongba Company's voluntary guarantee in the mediation agreement, it should have a relatively clear understanding of its own conduct in the case, so it could be determined that Tongba Company had engaged in the sale of the allegedly infringing product.

In summary, Tongba Company engaged in the sale of the allegedly infringing product, but there was no evidence to prove that it had engaged in production or offering for sale. The first-instance court's determination that the notarially sealed allegedly infringing baby carriage model was TBT86, its comparison with the patent in question, and its finding that it fell within the scope of protection of the patent in question, had a factual and legal basis.

(II) How to determine Tongba Company's civil liability

The parties had previously reached a mediation agreement under the auspices of the People's Court in a patent infringement dispute, and the agreement stipulated that the condition for compensating economic losses was that Tongba Company had engaged in new infringing acts. Therefore, whether the infringing act was established was the basis for the rights and obligations of the parties in this case, and the content of the mediation agreement could not be directly used as the basis for the rights and obligations of the parties.

On September 2, 2009, Tongba Company and Longcheng Company reached a mediation agreement in the previous patent infringement case. The allegedly infringing baby carriage product model in that case was B858C-B. The agreement stipulated that "if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's design patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates 500,000 yuan; if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates 1,000,000 yuan." As for the content of this agreement, since it specifically targeted the allegedly infringing product model B858C-B, and not the allegedly infringing product TBT86 in this case, the amount of compensation stipulated in the mediation agreement could not apply to this case where the product models were different. Moreover, the existing evidence only indicated that Tongba Company had engaged in sales infringement. Therefore, the determination of the amount of patent infringement compensation could not ignore the actual circumstances of this case, especially the value share of the patent in question in the overall vehicle, and the fact that the allegedly infringing product itself had not entered the market for sale, whether domestically or internationally; furthermore, there was no direct evidence to show that Tongba Company had engaged in the "still large-scale and uninterrupted engagement in acts infringing the patent right in question" alleged by Longcheng Company. Therefore, the first-instance court's discretion to order Tongba Company to compensate Longcheng Company for economic losses of 140,000 yuan in accordance with Article 65 of the Patent Law was consistent with the actual circumstances of this case. Longcheng Company's request to directly determine the amount of compensation based on the mediation agreement lacked factual and legal basis, and the court did not support it.

Regarding the burden of case acceptance fees in the first instance. Article 29 of the "Measures for Payment of Litigation Fees" provides that litigation fees shall be borne by the losing party, unless the winning party voluntarily assumes them. In the case of partial victory and partial defeat, the People's Court shall determine the amount of litigation fees to be borne by each party based on the specific circumstances of the case. The first-instance court, based on the specific circumstances of this case and having found that Tongba Company's infringement was established, decided that Tongba Company should bear all the case acceptance fees in the first instance, which had a factual and legal basis. Tongba Company's appeal reason that the first-instance court's decision to make it bear all the case acceptance fees was unfair was not sustainable.

In summary, Longcheng Company's appeal request and reasons were all untenable and were dismissed in accordance with the law. Tongba Company's reason that it did not produce the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement was established, and the first-instance court's finding in this regard was erroneous and was corrected in accordance with the law; Tongba Company's other appeal requests and reasons were untenable and were dismissed in accordance with the law. The first-instance judgment had clear factual findings, correct application of law, and proper substantive handling, and should be upheld in accordance with the law. The court of second instance ruled: dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. The case acceptance fee for the second instance was 13,800 yuan, with Longcheng Company bearing 11,040 yuan and Tongba Company bearing 2,760 yuan.

Longcheng Company, refusing to accept the second-instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, claiming: (A) The second-instance court made errors in fact-finding. 1. Tongba Company did not deny that the allegedly infringing product was produced by it, and the second-instance court's finding in this regard was erroneous. 2. The facts of Tongba Company's offering for sale of the allegedly infringing product were clear, and the second-instance court's finding in this regard was erroneous. (B) The second-instance court applied the law incorrectly. 1. The second-instance court failed to apply the compensation standard stipulated in the Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 42, which constituted an error in the application of law. In this case, which is a patent infringement dispute, the first-instance court, when determining the assumption of civil compensation liability, cited Article 122 of the Contract Law and held that determining the amount of compensation in accordance with the Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 42 would conflict with the provisions of the Contract Law, and therefore did not support it. The second-instance court also did not correct the first-instance court's error in this regard. The first three methods of determining the amount of compensation provided for in Article 65 of the Patent Law all rely on evidence provided unilaterally by the parties during litigation, whereas the civil mediation document in this case is a judicial confirmation of the consensus of both parties. Applying the civil mediation document to determine liability for compensation in this case would not conflict with the provisions of the Patent Law and the Contract Law. 2. The second-instance court's rejection of the application of the compensation standard stipulated in the mediation document on the grounds that the allegedly infringing product model "TBT86" in this case was different from the infringing product model "B858C-B" involved in the previous case was clearly erroneous. Compared with the previous case, as long as there is evidence to prove that Tongba Company again implemented an infringing act, the condition for compensation stipulated in the mediation document has been satisfied. Longcheng Company applied for retrial in accordance with Paragraph (2) and Item (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting this Court to revoke the first-instance and second-instance judgments, amend the judgment to support its claims raised in the first instance, and order Tongba Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Tongba Company submitted its opinion stating: (A) The second-instance court's fact-finding was clear. 1. The second-instance court's finding that Tongba Company did not engage in the production of the allegedly infringing product was clear. 2. The second-instance court's finding that Tongba Company did not engage in the offering for sale of the allegedly infringing product was clear. (B) The second-instance court applied the law correctly. 1. The People's Court had the right to determine whether the compensation calculation method set in the mediation document should be adopted in this case based on the handling principles for concurrence of liability stipulated in Article 122 of the Contract Law, and the second-instance court applied the law correctly. This case is an infringement lawsuit initiated by Longcheng Company, and the amount of compensation should be determined in accordance with the compensation methods provided for in the tort law. When tort liability and contractual liability concur, Longcheng Company could choose to file a tort lawsuit or a breach of contract lawsuit to protect its rights, but after choosing a tort lawsuit, it could no longer claim compensation for breach of contract based on the mediation document. Longcheng Company's request to determine liability for compensation in this case in accordance with the method for calculating the amount of compensation stipulated in the mediation document essentially seeks to claim liability for breach of contract in a tort lawsuit, which violates the handling principles for concurrence of civil liability. 2. The Patent Law does not provide for compensation agreed upon in advance. The first-instance and second-instance courts determined the amount of compensation in accordance with the statutory compensation method provided for in Article 65 of the Patent Law. At the same time, when applying statutory compensation, they considered factors such as Tongba Company's subjective fault for repeated infringement and appropriately increased the severity of compensation sanctions against Tongba Company. The amount of compensation determined was reasonable and appropriate, and the application of law was correct. 3. The second-instance court's determination that the amount of compensation stipulated in the mediation document could not apply to this case on the grounds that the allegedly infringing product model in this case was different from the infringing product model involved in the mediation document was clear in fact-finding and correct in the application of law.

This Court found upon trial that the facts found by the first-instance and second-instance courts were substantially true and were confirmed by this Court.

This Court also found:

(I) Circumstances of the prior case and the civil mediation document

In April 2008, Longcheng Company filed three lawsuits with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that the baby carriages produced and sold by Tongba Company infringed Longcheng Company's patent rights.

In the case of Longcheng Company v. Tongba Company for infringement of the "Baby Carriage Folding Joint" design patent (Patent No. ZL02322197.6), the infringing product involved was the D900 model baby carriage. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Zhi Chu Zi No. 143, finding infringement established and ordering Tongba Company to cease infringement and assume liability for compensation. After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed.

In the case of Longcheng Company v. Tongba Company for infringement of the "Baby Carriage Single-Hand Folding Structure" utility model patent (Patent No. ZL00228933.4), the infringing product involved was the D900 model baby carriage. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Zhi Chu Zi No. 142, finding infringement established and ordering Tongba Company to cease infringement and assume liability for compensation. Tongba Company appealed the first-instance judgment to the Hubei High People's Court. During the second-instance proceedings, the parties voluntarily reached a mediation agreement, the main content of which was: 1. Tongba Company shall immediately cease manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling the D900 model baby carriage product from the date of signing the mediation agreement, remove pictures of this model baby carriage product from Tongba Company's website and introductions to this model product in product brochures, and guarantee not to infringe Longcheng Company's patent rights in the future. If one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's design patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates RMB 500,000; if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates RMB 1,000,000; 2. Tongba Company shall compensate Longcheng Company for economic losses of RMB 55,000 within ten days from the date of signing the mediation agreement, and pay the first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 3,300 and evidence preservation fee of RMB 30 advanced by Longcheng Company; 3. Both parties waive other claims based on the facts of this case. After examining and confirming the mediation agreement, the Hubei High People's Court issued Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 41 on September 2, 2009.

In the case of Longcheng Company v. Tongba Company for infringement of the "Front Wheel Positioning Device" utility model patent (Patent No. ZL01242571.0), the infringing product involved was the B858C-B model baby carriage. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Zhi Chu Zi No. 144, finding infringement established and ordering Tongba Company to cease infringement and assume liability for compensation. Tongba Company appealed the first-instance judgment to the Hubei High People's Court. During the second-instance proceedings, the parties voluntarily reached a mediation agreement, the content of which was consistent with the mediation agreement confirmed by Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 41, except that the infringing baby carriage product model involved changed from D900 to B858C-B. After examining and confirming the mediation agreement, the Hubei High People's Court issued Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 42 on September 2, 2009.

(II) Circumstances concerning the interpretation of the mediation agreement

Regarding the stipulation in the mediation agreement that "if one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates RMB 1,000,000," Longcheng Company argued at the trial of this Court that "one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right" refers to an act infringing one of Longcheng Company's utility model patent rights, which is neither limited to the specific model of infringing product in the prior case nor limited to the utility model patent right involved in the prior case; if "several" utility model patent rights are infringed, it constitutes "several" acts of infringement. Tongba Company argued in its written defense submitted to this Court that "one act of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right" is aimed at the relevant infringing acts concerning the specific model of infringing product in the prior case; later, at the trial of this Court, it argued that, based on the literal meaning of the mediation agreement, the relevant infringing acts should not be limited to the specific model of infringing product in the prior case, and if other products outside the case constitute infringement of utility model patent rights, they also satisfy the conditions stipulated in the mediation agreement.

This Court is of the opinion that, considering the retrial applicant's reasons for applying for retrial and the respondent's defense, the focus of the dispute in this case is: whether Tongba Company engaged in the acts of manufacturing and offering for sale the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement; and how to determine Tongba Company's liability for compensation.

(I) Whether Tongba Company engaged in the act of manufacturing the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement

In the first-instance proceedings, to prove that Tongba Company again engaged in the act of manufacturing the allegedly infringing product, Longcheng Company submitted to the court Notarial Certificate (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi No. 125, the sales settlement slip issued by Tongba Company, and the notarially sealed allegedly infringing product. Since Notarial Certificate (2010) Chuan Zheng Zi No. 125 and the sales settlement slip could only prove that Tongba Company sold the allegedly infringing product on March 9, 2010, but could not prove the time when Tongba Company manufactured the allegedly infringing product, and the results of the inspection at the first-instance trial could not prove that Tongba Company engaged in the act of manufacturing the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement, therefore, in accordance with Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 2, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," the second-instance court's finding that there was no evidence to prove that Tongba Company engaged in the act of manufacturing the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement was not improper. Longcheng Company's reason for applying for retrial in this regard cannot be established, and this Court does not support it.

(II) Whether Tongba Company engaged in the act of offering for sale the allegedly infringing product after signing the mediation agreement

In the first-instance proceedings, to prove that Tongba Company again engaged in the act of offering for sale the allegedly infringing product, Longcheng Company submitted to the court Notarial Certificate (2009) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 5846, Notarial Certificate (2010) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 938, the "List of Exhibitors for the China Import and Export Fair," and Tongba Company's "Product Brochure."

Since the webpage screenshots in Notarial Certificate (2009) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 5846 and Notarial Certificate (2010) Zhongzheng Nei Zi No. 938 did not contain relevant content about the allegedly infringing product TBT86 baby carriage in this case, and the "List of Exhibitors for the China Import and Export Fair" only listed Tongba Company's name, address, and contact information, without product information, the above evidence could not prove that Tongba Company engaged in the act of offering for sale the allegedly infringing product.

Regarding the evidence "Product Brochure," Tongba Company raised no objections to its authenticity, legality, or relevance during the first-instance evidentiary proceedings. Based on this, the first-instance court compared the baby carriage physically preserved through notarization with the picture of the baby carriage in the "Product Brochure" during trial, thereby determining that the accused infringing product in this case was the TBT86 model. However, on the other hand, the first-instance court also held that "the 'Product Brochure' only contains several photographs and brief textual descriptions of the baby carriages, making it impossible to compare the technical features such as the shape, structure, and combination methods of the baby carriages with the claims of the patent-in-suit," and consequently did not find Tongba Company's act of offering for sale to constitute infringement. This reasoning is internally contradictory. Regarding this issue, the court of second instance held that "the source of the 'Product Brochure' is unclear and its printing time is unknown," and therefore did not find Tongba Company's act of offering for sale to constitute infringement. This Court holds: First, since the first-instance court had already compared the physically notarized baby carriage with the baby carriage picture in the "Product Brochure" during trial and accordingly determined that the accused infringing product in this case was the TBT86 model, it can be established that the "Product Brochure" contained sales and promotional information regarding the accused infringing product. Second, Tongba Company's opinion on the examination of the "Product Brochure" shows that it had no objections to the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the "Product Brochure"; thus, the reasoning that "the source is unclear" cannot stand. Third, the printing time of the "Product Brochure" is of no legal significance to the determination of whether Tongba Company offered for sale the accused infringing product after the execution of the mediation agreement. Even if the printing time was before the execution of the mediation agreement, it would not affect the characterization of the act of distributing or disseminating the "Product Brochure" after the execution of the mediation agreement as an offer for sale. Therefore, based on the comparison and inspection conducted by the first-instance court during trial and Tongba Company's opinion on the examination of the "Product Brochure," it can be established that Tongba Company offered for sale the accused infringing product after the execution of the mediation agreement. Longcheng Company's ground for retrial on this issue is valid and shall be upheld. The finding of the court of second instance on this issue was erroneous, and this Court hereby corrects it.

(3) How to Determine Tongba Company's Compensation Liability

1. Regarding the Validity of the Mediation Agreement Reached by the Parties in the Prior Case

Since the mediation agreement was voluntarily reached by both parties, its content involves only the disposition of private rights, does not involve public interests or the interests of third parties, and does not have any other circumstances of invalidity provided by law. Moreover, after reviewing and confirming the mediation agreement, the Hubei High People's Court issued a civil mediation document. Therefore, the mediation agreement reached by the parties in the prior case is legally valid.

2. Whether the Method for Determining the Amount of Compensation Agreed Upon by the Parties in the Mediation Agreement Can Be Applied in This Case

First, this Court holds that the civil liability to be borne by Tongba Company in this case does not constitute a scenario where tort liability and liability for breach of contract concur. The concurrence of tort liability and liability for breach of contract under Article 122 of the Contract Law requires the legal element that "a party's breach of contract infringes upon the other party's personal or property rights and interests." As per this provision, the prerequisite for the concurrence of liability for breach of contract and tort liability is the existence of a basic transactional contract relationship between the parties. Based on this transactional contract relationship, one party's breach of the obligations agreed upon in the contract, and such breach simultaneously infringes upon the other party's rights and interests, gives rise to tort liability. Therefore, the "breach of contract" in this provision refers to the violation of obligations under the basic transactional contract, and such breach simultaneously infringes upon the other party's rights and interests, but does not refer to the violation of an agreement made after the occurrence of the infringing act regarding how to bear compensation liability. The "breach of contract" and "tortious act" under Article 122 of the Contract Law refer to the same legal act, whereas a party's tortious act and the agreement by both parties after the occurrence of the tortious act regarding the method of calculation and amount of compensation liability are two separate legal acts. As to the content of the mediation agreement, it is not a basic transactional contract between Longcheng Company and Tongba Company, but rather an agreement on how to bear tort compensation liability (including the method of calculation and amount) after the occurrence of the tortious act. Therefore, the civil liability to be borne by Tongba Company in this case does not fall within the concurrence of tort liability and liability for breach of contract under Article 122 of the Contract Law.

Second, it should be clarified that the civil liability to be borne by Tongba Company in this case is tort liability. On one hand, as discussed above, there was no basic contract relationship between Longcheng Company and Tongba Company. On the other hand, the legal significance and effect of the mediation agreement are not to specify Tongba Company's contractual transaction obligations, but to specify how tort liability shall be borne. Even without the mediation agreement, Tongba Company is equally obligated not to infringe based on legal provisions. The purpose of including in the mediation agreement the specific method and amount of compensation for Tongba Company's future acts of infringement is merely to facilitate further agreement on how Tongba Company's tort liability shall be borne upon its re-infringement.

Third, laws such as the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China and the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China do not prohibit the infringed party and the infringer from pre-agreeing on the method of tort liability or the amount of tort compensation. The legal nature of such an agreement can be characterized as a simplified method of calculation and determination, pre-agreed by both parties, of the losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement or the profits gained by the infringer from infringement in the event of future infringement. This Court holds that, considering factors such as difficulties in evidence production and the time-consuming and costly nature of litigation, both parties are entirely free, within the realm of private autonomy, to agree on the amount of compensation for infringement. Such agreement includes both post-infringement agreements and pre-infringement agreements. Therefore, applying the method for determining the amount of compensation agreed upon by the parties in the mediation agreement to this case does not conflict with the relevant provisions of Article 65 of the Patent Law. It is noteworthy that Paragraph 3 of Article 25 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Copyright stipulates that if both parties reach an agreement on the amount of compensation based on the right holder's actual losses or the infringer's illegal gains, the court shall permit it. This provision represents the court's recognition of a "post-agreement" reached by the parties on the amount of compensation for tort liability involved in the case.

In summary, the method for determining the amount of compensation agreed upon by Longcheng Company and Tongba Company in the mediation agreement can be applied in this case.

3. How to Apply the Method for Determining the Amount of Compensation Agreed Upon by the Parties in the Mediation Agreement in This Case

How to specifically apply the method for determining the amount of compensation agreed upon in the mediation agreement in this case depends on the interpretation of the following clause in the mediation agreement: "If one instance of infringement of Longcheng Company's utility model patent right is discovered, Tongba Company voluntarily compensates RMB 1,000,000." According to the facts ascertained by this Court, the cases involved in Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 41 and Civil Mediation Document (2009) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 42 were both cases of infringement of utility model patent rights. However, the mediation agreements also contained terms prohibiting Tongba Company from further infringing upon Longcheng Company's design patent rights and utility model patent rights. Considering that multiple patent infringement disputes have occurred between Longcheng Company and Tongba Company, and the opinions expressed by both parties on this issue during the trial of this case, it can be established that the provisions in the mediation agreement regarding Tongba Company's prohibition of further infringement and the corresponding amount of compensation constitute a package agreement. That is: First, the "one instance of infringement" in the above clause is not limited to the specific model of infringing baby carriage involved in the prior case. Second, the "one instance of infringement" in the above clause is not limited to the patent right involved in the prior case. Third, the "one instance of infringement" in the above clause refers to an act of infringing one patent right of Longcheng Company. Therefore, Tongba Company shall compensate Longcheng Company RMB 1,000,000 in this case. Longcheng Company's ground for retrial on this issue is valid and shall be upheld. The court of second instance applied the law erroneously in determining Tongba Company's compensation liability, and this error shall be corrected.

In conclusion, this Court holds that the second-instance judgment's finding that Tongba Company did not offer for sale the accused infringing product after the execution of the mediation agreement was erroneous in fact and shall be corrected. The second-instance judgment's discretion to award Longcheng Company RMB 140,000 as compensation was erroneous in law and shall be corrected. Pursuant to Article 65, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 207, Paragraph 1 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2012) E Min San Zhong Zi No. 86 of the Hubei High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2011) Wu Zhi Chu Zi No. 467 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province;

2. Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days from the date of service of this judgment, compensate Zhongshan Longcheng Daily Products Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 1,000,000.

If the pecuniary obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 13,800 and property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 13,800, shall be borne by Hubei Tongba Children's Products Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Chuang
Acting Judge: Zhu Li
Acting Judge: He Peng

December 7, 2013
